selected_problem: After evidence revision freshness was restored, open-ended candidate discovery still truncated to the first 16 actionable boundary rows before DWAC ranking. Sixteen recent low-severity NO CLAIM boundaries could therefore exclude a later higher-severity UNRESOLVED boundary that was already inside the 96-row observation budget.

execution.route_basis: single evidence-rich high-centrality autonomous diagnosis defect

changes: Truth-boundary candidates are now stably ordered by explicit marker severity before the 16-candidate budget is applied.
Equal-severity boundaries preserve observation order, so evidence recency remains the tie-breaker established by the previous cycle.
Externally blocked boundaries remain behind actionable internal boundaries and are severity-ordered only within the blocked partition.
A focused regression proves that sixteen NO CLAIM rows can no longer hide a later UNRESOLVED row from DWAC diagnosis.

validation.pre_fix_regression: FAIL_AS_EXPECTED: selected No claim 0 and excluded the later UNRESOLVED boundary

truth_boundaries: Marker severity is a diagnosis priority signal, not proof that an older boundary remains semantically open after newer code changes.
Equal-severity ties preserve the revision-aware observation order from the fresh-evidence cycle.
The candidate budget remains bounded at 16 and the observation row budget remains bounded at 96.
